**7B.5 Research Note**
Mixed, leaning negative. Modi’s 2024 government did keep some technocratic staffing in core economic posts, but the year also shows strong signs of opaque donor networks, coalition patronage, and business-political entanglement. I did not find reliable 2024 evidence of close family members being placed in office or of a direct family-enrichment vehicle.

**Positive / mitigating evidence**
- **Indian government appoints members for new Finance Commission panel** | Reuters via Investing.com | 30 Jan 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/indian-government-appoints-members-for-new-finance-panel-3287402 | Claim: The panel included former expenditure officials, a policy executive, SBI’s chief economic adviser, and economist Arvind Panagariya as chair, which supports professional staffing of a key fiscal institution. | IDs: 7B.5
- **India names Sanjay Malhotra to replace Das as central bank governor** | Reuters via ThePrint | 9 Dec 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/india-names-sanjay-malhotra-to-replace-das-as-central-bank-governor/2394973 | Claim: Modi’s government chose a career IAS officer with finance, taxation, IT, and revenue experience for RBI governor, a technocratic appointment rather than an obvious loyalist pick. | IDs: 7B.5
- **Indias Modi prevails over allies in cabinet line-up** | Reuters via ThePrint | 11 Jun 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-prevails-over-allies-in-cabinet-line-up/2126130/ | Claim: Modi kept key ministries, including senior economic portfolios, in the same hands after the election setback, which is weak evidence of continuity and some competence retention. | IDs: 7B.5
- **India’s finance minister unveils budget with focus on poor, women, youth and farmers** | Reuters via ThePrint | 1 Feb 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/indias-finance-minister-unveils-budget-with-focus-on-poor-women-youth-and-farmers/1948406/ | Claim: The interim budget explicitly centered disadvantaged groups and avoided a classic pre-poll giveaway, which is a limited signal of programmatic rather than purely factional spending. | IDs: 7B.5
- **PM Modi declares total assets worth Rs 3.02 crore in poll affidavit** | The Economic Times / Reuters | 14 May 2024 | https://m.economictimes.com/news/elections/lok-sabha/india/pm-modi-declares-total-assets-worth-rs-3-02-crore-in-poll-affidavit/amp_articleshow/110119535.cms | Claim: Modi’s affidavit disclosure is a transparency signal and weak counterevidence to hidden personal enrichment, though it does not rule out conflicts of interest. | IDs: 7B.5; 7B.4

**Negative / concerning evidence**
- **Explainer: what were India’s electoral bonds and how did they power Modi’s party?** | Reuters via ThePrint | 16 Feb 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/explainer-what-were-indias-electoral-bonds-and-how-did-they-power-modis-party/1969006/ | Claim: Reuters described unlimited anonymous political donations that heavily benefited the BJP, showing opaque finance and capture risk around the ruling party. | IDs: 7B.5; 7B.4
- **Obscure trust links India’s top businesses with Modi’s election war chest** | Reuters via ThePrint | 12 Apr 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/obscure-trust-links-indias-top-businesses-with-modi-s-election-war-chest-2/2038095/ | Claim: A major electoral trust reportedly routed about 75% of its donations to the BJP, suggesting concentrated business-linked political access. | IDs: 7B.5; 7B.4
- **Qwik, a top buyer of Indian electoral bonds, is affiliated to Ambani’s Reliance, filings show** | Reuters via ThePrint | 15 Mar 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/qwik-a-top-buyer-of-indian-electoral-bonds-is-affiliated-to-ambani-s-reliance-filings-show/2002426/ | Claim: A Reliance-affiliated company bought large volumes of electoral bonds, reinforcing concerns about privileged business proximity to ruling-party finance. | IDs: 7B.5; 7B.4
- **Modi’s allies want funds, cabinet jobs as coalition talks begin** | Reuters via Investing.com | 6 Jun 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/modis-appeal-clouded-in-india-election-by-prices-jobs-graft-survey-says-3472931 | Claim: Coalition partners immediately demanded funds and cabinet positions, which is classic patronage bargaining rather than clean merit-based staffing. | IDs: 7B.5; 7B.4
- **Indias Modi spends billions on jobs, key allies in first budget after election** | Reuters via ThePrint | 23 Jul 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-spends-billions-on-jobs-key-allies-in-first-budget-after-election/2187546/ | Claim: The post-election budget directed more than $5 billion to coalition-led states and was explicitly framed as a way to win back voters and retain support. | IDs: 7B.5; 7B.4
- **Indian opposition calls for Adani probe, Modi’s BJP questions timing of U.S. indictment** | Reuters via ThePrint | 21 Nov 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/indian-opposition-calls-for-adani-probe-modis-bjp-questions-timing-of-us-indictment/2367046/ | Claim: After Adani’s U.S. bribery indictment, opposition parties alleged Modi’s government protected the conglomerate, which is allegation-based but relevant to cronies-and-protection concerns. | IDs: 7B.5; 7B.4
- **Bribe notes with per-megawatt rates filings detail Sagar Adani’s role in Indian scandal** | Reuters via ThePrint | 25 Nov 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/bribe-notes-with-per-megawatt-rates-filings-detail-sagar-adanis-role-in-indian-scandal-2/2373372/ | Claim: Court filings described “bribe notes” tied to power-contract deals, a strong 2024 indicator of quid-pro-quo risk in Modi’s business orbit even if not direct proof of personal benefit. | IDs: 7B.5; 7B.4

**Gap**
- I did not find solid 2024 evidence that Modi’s close family directly received offices, contracts, gifts, or hidden-foundation benefits.
- The strongest negative case is therefore indirect: opaque party finance, coalition patronage, and repeated proximity to powerful business interests, rather than a documented family self-dealing scheme.
